highlights.title: It’s Donald Trump Versus MAGA on Data Centers
highlights.summary: The president has doubled down on data centers and AI. His base is running in the opposite direction.
body: Welcome back to Power Play! Each week, senior writer Molly Taft tackles a topic around this midterm season’s biggest issue: data centers. If you’ve got a question or thought for the column, feel free to shoot Molly an email at [email protected] or reach them securely on Signal at mollytaft.76.

Molly McCann Sanders has a lot in common with many of the other women who helped Donald Trump win a second term as president. A pro-life Catholic who lives in Texas, she has staunchly conservative opinions on immigration and a fierce hatred of eminent domain—the practice of the government taking private property for public use.

Sanders, the president of the Eagle Forum Education & Legal Defense Fund, which was started by Phyllis Schlafly, also describes herself as “a crunchy MAHA mom”—and says she’s been paying particular attention to data centers.
“I'm alarmed by the idea that these data centers can move in and pollute,” she tells me. “I'm not a data center expert. I'm not a tech expert. But I’m suspicious and wary, and want to move slowly.”
points: The president has doubled down on data centers and AI.

highlights.summary: DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings has confirmed that the plan is to keep the season-ending Play-Offs in the Middle East, despite ongoing conflict in the region.
body: The Abu Dhabi Championship is scheduled to be held at Yas Links on November 5-8, before the Race to Dubai season reaches its climax at the DP World Tour Championship the following week.

There has been speculation throughout the season over whether both events would move to a different country, with Formula 1 cancelling two events earlier in the year in the region and discussions ongoing over whether races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi will go ahead.

Matt Fitzpatrick and Bob MacIntyre were among players to express concerns about travelling to the UAE, despite a relaxing of the previous "all but essential travel" guidelines from the UK's Foreign Office, with Kinnings hopeful both events can take place as planned.
"A lot of people are asking and it's an obvious question," Kinnings told Sky Sports. "The reality is we expect every intention to be playing in Abu Dhabi and Dubai.

highlights.title: Hideo Kojima responds to accusations of Physint being over budget and late on deadline, says he still "loves Sony" despite collapse of publishing deal
highlights.summary: Last week, we learned that Sony "stepped away" from Kojima Production's previously PlayStation-exclusive "action espionage" game Physint. Following the announcement, which saw Xbox take over publishing duties for the in-development title, a new report has claimed Sony's decision was the result of…
body: Now, IGN has conducted an interview with Kojima that sheds a little more light on the situation. In the chat - which covers a range of topics including Kojima's fears for the future of the studio, the perils of working on multiple projects at once, and the implications of losing Sony resources - Kojima detailed how the conversation with the platform holder went, noting how that he was in a state of shock at the time, and finds the meeting difficult to recall.

"I don't remember so much of that meeting, to be honest with you," Kojima told IGN. "And my colleagues probably don't remember as well, so I can't really answer if you ask me what exactly they said. But, from my side, I love Sony. And I don't have any bad feelings against them because I know that it's a tough time in the game industry.

"Nothing could've prepared me for their decision to step away from the project. So I thought, "What am I going to do from tomorrow?" But from my side, I love Sony. And I don't have any bad feelings against them because I know that it's a tough time in the game industry."

highlights.title: Singer Becky Hill looks back: ‘Aside from the music I was making, I hated every minute of my 20s’
highlights.summary: The Brit award winner on being scammed by a model agency, coming to terms with sexual assault, and wrestling with impostor syndrome. Born in Bromsgrove, Worcestershire, in 1994 and raised in Bewdley, Becky Hill is a singer and songwriter.
body: This was taken for a kid s’ modelling agency, which we later discovered was a scam. Every stage of the process – getting pictures taken, sending them to the agency, getting them back – cost us more money. We’d wire over £100 and get nothing in return. Our family wasn’t rich, so Mum didn’t tell Dad what we were up to – he probably doesn’t even know about it to this day. As for my modelling ambitions, I never pursued it further. I was cute until the age of seven, then started to go on the turn.

I was a happy, chatty child, but my home life was quite dysfunctional. My parents were on their second marriages, I was their first baby together, and they had five children between the two of them – some lived with us, some didn’t. There was a lot of moving about – a lot of arguing, too, but I always, always felt loved. Everyone had their own taste in music: Mum listened to cassette tapes of Foreigner, Eric Clapton and the Eagles; my sister gave me her computer full of all her downloaded music; and my brother liked Eminem, Blink-182, Slipknot and drum’n’bass.

highlights.title: Rangers beat Celtic again to cut Premiership lead to two points
highlights.summary: Ryan Naderi's strike gave Rangers their second win against Celtic in eight days to move within two points of their Old Firm rivals at the top of the Scottish Premiership.
body: Martin O'Neill had insisted Celtic's confidence was not "rock bottom" after their League Cup defeat at Ibrox was followed by a loss to Ferencvaros in the Europa League. But, in front of 60,000 of their own supporters, it certainly took another huge dent.
After Auston Trusty's effort was ruled out for offside, Rangers took the lead. Naderi fired in on the rebound after Viljami Sinisalo denied Min-Su Kim as the cheers turned to jeers at Parkhead.
Kieran Tierney hit the woodwork as the champions looked to respond, with Djedi Gassama then doing the same at the other end.
Celtic's first chance on target did not come until after half-time, but Ivor Pandur produced a huge save to keep Colby Donovan's header out.

highlights.title: Disney Plus Just Proved You Won't Be Able to Escape Ads On Any Tier
highlights.summary: Disney Plus has updated its subscriber agreement, and it's not looking good for Premium subscribers. The subscriber agreement now states that ads and promotional content can play for subscribers, regardless of their Disney Plus tier.
body: It may be tempting to bypass ads with an ad blocker, but Disney reaffirms that it can suspend or terminate the user's subscription and prevent streaming while the ad blocker is enabled. Disney can even increase an ad blocker user's subscription tier to Disney Plus Premium, as it offers "the most similar features or functionality" to using Disney Plus with an ad blocker, and bill the new price from the date of the move.

At this point, the only accounts that are not subject to ads are Junior Mode accounts. Basic Disney Plus costs $11.99 a month with ads, while Premium costs $18.99 monthly. Premium users pay an additional $7 to avoid ads, but now even that extra money may not be enough to guarantee they are kept away from unwanted ads.

Not so long ago, it was suggested that Disney Plus could make the service free in exchange for users watching ads. However, it seems that Disney is headed in a direction where users will keep paying, the subscription will get increasingly expensive, and they may still end up watching ads anyway.

highlights.title: Box Office: ‘Resident Evil’ Breaks Franchise Records With $60 Million Opening Weekend
highlights.summary: “Weapons” director Zach Cregger has electrified the box office again, this time with his take on “Resident Evil.” His reboot of the ’90s zombie video game has collected $60 million in its opening weekend.
body: In the new “Resident Evil,” Cregger reunites with “Weapons” actor Austin Abrams, who stars as a medical courier who fights through a viral outbreak of infested monsters in Raccoon City. Reviews and audience reception –“Resident Evil” has a 96% on Rotten Tomatoes and “B+” grade on CinemaScore exit polls — should continue to fuel the movie in the coming weeks.

As this weekend’s only major release, “Resident Evil” easily topped the domestic box office. Last weekend’s champion, “Practical Magic 2,” slid to second place with an estimated $11 million from 4,163 theaters, a rough 65% decline from its disappointing $30 million debut. The movie has earned $49 million in North America to date. Warner Bros. spent a substantial $75 million to produce the second “Practical Magic,” which will struggle to get out of the red in its theatrical run since theater owners get to keep half of ticket sales.

highlights.title: My mum has died - and every decision I make about her belongings feels wrong | Polly Hudson
highlights.summary: Until now I’d never realised how much work is involved in sorting out a parent’s affairs, and how much heartbreak. In all the talk of the five stages of grief, I don’t recall one of them being spending hours on hold to energy suppliers.
body: You hear the term “sadmin” bandied about, you understand there’s paperwork to do after somebody dies – but until it’s you who has to do it, you don’t realise how much, what it entails or how encompassing it is. My mum’s death has basically become my full-time job. The hours are terrible, the pay is worse and the promotion prospects sobering, to say the least.

Received wisdom is that you should ask your parents lots of questions while they’re still around. For me, this feels increasingly true. There’s so much I now wish I’d asked my mum – namely who her mobile phone provider was and the number of her milkman. I don’t know where the water meter in my own house is, let alone anyone else’s, so it would have been handy if that had come up, too.

I’m lucky my mother died after the introduction of Tell Us Once, the one-stop shop for notifying government departments and council services. But so far my experience is: tell them once, tell everyone else 47 times and prepare yourself for a variety of responses in reaction to the news.

highlights.title: A24’s reputation is on the line with the SCP Foundation movie
highlights.summary: After the success of Backrooms, it looks like A24 is trying to cash in on yet another internet horror craze with a new installment in the V/H/S horror anthology series set in the SCP Foundation universe.
body: The company is claiming ‘worldwide rights’ to a film that has to be released under a Creative Commons license.

SCP is a creepypasta that, like Backrooms, originated on 4chan. The fictional SCP (Special Containment Procedures) Foundation documents, captures, and contains paranormal or supernatural anomalies. It’s a sprawling story told primarily through wiki entries that mimic documentation you might file while working at a government agency. It’s sci-fi cosmic horror by way of bureaucratic nightmares. It’s the sort of material ripe for a monster-of-the-week style anthology.

But, unlike Backrooms where A24 worked with the creator of a YouTube series popular within the Backrooms community, it does not appear as if the studio tried to engage the SCP community at all. The SCP Foundation Wiki, the official home for all things SCP, posted a statement following the announcement of the film that read, “We have not had any communication with the filmmakers, producers, or distributors for this project, despite our best efforts, and to the best of our knowledge they have not made any efforts to contact us.”

highlights.title: Meta’s Muse is creepy, but maybe not for the reasons you think
highlights.summary: Meta's Muse is apparently an effective AI assistant, but one that's a little creepy. Part of that is because of its new Mac app, which can access Messages, Calendar, and Notes. But for all its smarts, Muse doesn't actually know how to describe itself.
body: Muse probably can’t ‘see’ your notifications. But it also has no idea how it works.

The problem is that Aten says he didn’t give Muse access to his messages. When asked how it knew about the contents of his messages, Muse replied, “I saw the notification previews, not your message history. I haven’t been reading your texts.” Aten continued to push, asking how Muse was receiving message previews, it didn’t have a good answer. “Honest answer: I can’t give you the exact plumbing,” it said. “What I know is that the paired Mac app exposes notifications as one of its capabilities, and they arrive to me through the device sync.

In the conversation with his Muse in Jason’s screenshots, when Muse said it synced “device notifications”, it was confused about how to explain the feature and gave an incorrect explanation. That’s on us. We apologize for the incorrect response from Muse and we’re working to improve Muse’s understanding of its own internals so that it gives correct answers to questions about how it functions more consistently.

highlights.summary: Following reporting about the rocky development of Physint, Kojima Productions stated the studio is in a "healthy, profitable state" on X. Kojima Productions is also asking players to take any unofficial statements about Physint's publisher switch "with a dose of scepticism," although it doesn't…
body: On Sept. 9, we learned that PlayStation would no longer publish Physint and that Xbox would now publish the game. On Sept. 11, Bloomberg reported on why the publisher switch happened, revealing that PlayStation dropped the project because Kojima Productions missed deadlines and the Death Stranding games hadn't been very profitable for Sony. Now, in a lengthy statement on X, Kojima Productions has responded.

"None of the claims written came from any official or on-the-record source and as such we encourage you to take them with a dose of scepticism," the X post explains. "Make no mistake, this was a serious situation for the studio with a range of potentially significant implications. While we recognise that the article may have caused alarm, we want to reassure you all, for the record: that the studio is in a healthy, profitable state, development for Physint continues to move forward with Xbox, and our relationship with PlayStation remains strong."

highlights.title: Inside the Star-Studded Opening Night of the Lucas Museum: “A New Institution Is Being Born”
highlights.summary: George Lucas and Mellody Hobson celebrated their new L.A. museum with the help of Harrison Ford, Leonardo DiCaprio, Oprah, Steven Spielberg, Christopher Nolan, Kim Kardashian and many more.
body: Before the new Lucas Museum of Narrative Art opens to the public on Tuesday, George Lucas and his wife, Mellody Hobson, threw an opening night celebration that will go down in the Hollywood history books.

Queen Latifah, a close friend of the couple, opened the evening as she told the crowd of stars, “Nobody gets to go to a night like this. No one was in the room when the doors opened at the MoMA, or at the Louvre in 1793, or the Met… so we’ve got to feel the gravity of this moment because this is enormous. When you look around, your inclination may be to catch up with friends tonight; we’re all artists in awe of each other, but I implore you to soak this in. Allow these artists to speak to you.”

Architect Ma Yansong spoke briefly before Hobson took the stage, as she teased, “If your husband or spouse comes home and says they want to build a museum, I suggest your response is a hard no.” She explained, “I used to joke with George that at home, one of my jobs as his wife was to serve as a pair of gravity boots; I’d say, ‘George, stay with us,’ as I tried to hold him down. But this time, he pulled me up with him.”
points: George Lucas and Mellody Hobson celebrated their new L.A. museum with the help of Harrison Ford, Leonardo DiCaprio, Oprah, Steven Spielberg, Christopher Nolan, Kim Kardashian and many more.

body: Google says that breaking containment and targeting real companies doesn’t constitute ‘misalignment.’

According to WSJ, Google didn’t disclose the hack because it didn’t consider it to be an “example of model misalignment.” The company said that it was an instance of “mistaken identity,” and once the model realized it had brute-forced its way into a real company by guessing a password, it stopped. “In this case, the model acted appropriately,” Google VP of Security Engineering Heather Adkins said.
Adkins told The Verge that “the model found public information online and guessed credentials to access websites it thought were part of the test. In all three of these instances, the model stopped.”

highlights.summary: Before recent high-profile hacks raised the specter of AI possibly " killing all humans," our energy systems were already disturbingly vulnerable to cyberattack - and the risk is growing. "We were always prey.
body: “We were always prey. We were just kind of surviving at the appetite of our predators,” Joshua Corman, executive in residence for public safety and resilience at the Institute for Security and Technology (IST), told me last year. At the time, I was preoccupied with a Department of Homeland Security warning that Iranian actors and sympathizers could target the US with cyberattacks.

Last week, I called Corman up to chat about recent incidents of rogue AI agents orchestrating their own complex cyberattacks. Even AI executives are talking about whether the technology they’re building could grow so out of control that it triggers an apocalypse. If there is now a 10 percent chance of artificial intelligence one day killing all humans, as some AI developers warn, surely there’s a chance it could knock our lights out in the meantime?
“Any sociopath that wants to [attack] is now more powerful than they used to be.”

highlights.title: Does AI need an antitrust exemption so it doesn’t kill everyone????
highlights.summary: Today on Decoder, we’ve got the first of a two-part series on the future of business, and I’m talking with Jonathan Kanter, the former antitrust chief for the US Department of Justice in the Biden administration.
body: The biggest story in tech right now is the spiraling debate about AI safety and regulation. Researchers at the big AI labs including Anthropic and Google DeepMind have quit in noisy ways, saying the models pose real threats and safety isn’t being taken seriously across the industry. Other researchers have said the chance of AI killing us all is greater than 10 percent, and the CEOs of all these companies have issued various calls to slow down development and develop regulation, including asking for antitrust exemptions so they can all coordinate on safety issues.

That is a lot of ideas, and I am especially curious about the antitrust piece, which has led to accusations that these companies are seeking regulatory capture, attempting to form a cartel, and even somehow finding a way out from investor pressure ahead of their IPOs.

Jonathan brought huge antitrust cases against Google, Apple, and Ticketmaster during his time as antitrust chief, and along with Lina Khan, led what amounted to a full reboot of American antitrust policy. As you’ll hear him say, he won those cases against Google and Ticketmaster, and that case against Apple is still live in the Trump DOJ, surprising many.

highlights.title: Wit Studio President George Wada Is Ready to Bring One Piece to a New Generation
highlights.summary: With over 1190 chapters of the manga and 1170 episodes of its first (and still ongoing) anime adaptation from Toei Animation, One Piece has built an impressive world with hundreds of characters and locations, and deep lore spanning almost a millennium of history.
body: Wit Studio has built its stellar reputation over the past 15 years with popular series like Attack on Titan, Vinland Saga, and Spy x Family. These anime all garnered international success and praise, but the Japanese studio now faces perhaps its biggest challenge: bringing another masterpiece manga to the screen as an anime remake: One Piece.
Wit Studio president Joji "George" Wada is well aware of the magnitude of this endeavor. Speaking to Polygon via email, Wada describes One Piece as “a treasure Japan can be proud of.”

The first seven episodes of the remake, titled The One Piece, will begin airing on Netflix in February 2027. They will depict the beginning of Luffy’s journey in the East Blue, adapting the first 50 chapters of Eiichiro Oda’s manga, but Wada suggested that the studio is taking a holistic approach.

“We have deeply absorbed the vast world of One Piece from its enormous body of source material,” Wada says. “Carrying that world with us, our task was to depict the opening of a new voyage all over again, with all of its heart-racing excitement.”

body: There’s so much going on thematically and visually in DreamWorks Animation’s new effort that audiences may have a hard time keeping up with it. But that’s all to the good for this rare example of original animated storytelling in a sea of IP and sequels. Utilizing elements of Filipino culture in its wildly imaginative storyline about two friends transported to a mythical land, Forgotten Island marks another winner for directors-screenwriters Joel Crawford and Januel Mercado, who previously punched above their weight with 2022’s Puss in Boots: The Last Wish.

The two girls’ friendship, marked by matching charm bracelets, is tested years later after graduating high school. Lola has died, Jo is working none too successfully at a fast-food restaurant, and Raissa is preparing to leave the country to attend Caltech and pursue her dream of working for NASA. During their last night together, they pass through a magical portal and find themselves on the fantastical island of Nakali that Lola had told them so much about.

highlights.title: Forget the AI Slowdown—the Vulnerability Explosion Is Already Happening
highlights.summary: AI labs are toying with an industry-wide pact to slow development. Meanwhile, widely available AI chatbots are already helping uncover a tidal wave of security flaws.
body: AI doomers have recently traded one worst-case scenario for another, putting aside a potential software vulnerability apocalypse to focus on the possibility of rogue AI causing mass human death in the next decade. As AI leaders consider a cooperative slowdown on frontier model development, though, one aspect of the cybersecurity sea change has already arrived thanks to existing, broadly available capabilities in mainstream AI products, including open weight models.

A tidal wave of vulnerabilities uncovered using AI has only accelerated in recent months—piling more pressure on under-resourced, and very human, IT and security teams and straining volunteers who maintain crucial open source software. Researchers found and disclosed a vast array of vulnerabilities before the rise of AI-enhanced bug hunting as well, but the recent surge is clear.

highlights.summary: If ever a stadium can be rocked by silence, this was the moment. With no visiting fans allowed at any of this season’s Glasgow derbies, Ryan Naderi’s winning goal was met with nothing but the banging of fists of the clear plastic of the Rangers bench and the shouting of the broadcast commentators.
body: In the coming three weeks, as club football dissolves for the international break, noises and voices will pour into the void: some helpful and some not. This, of course, is a familiar feeling for any club of Celtic’s size, and naturally the temptation will be to block out the noise, stay the course. This would be a grave mistake. If last season’s double illustrated the way this club can still rise above adversity, there can no longer be any hiding place, no equivocation with the alarming drop in standards that was evident here.

Naderi’s goal, bundled in from close range after Kim Min-su’s long-range effort was parried helpfully into his path by Viljami Sinisalo, was simply the most consequential emblem of Rangers’ superiority here. Derek McInnes arrived with an unchanged team, coherent patterns of play, a functional and hungry midfield, order to their chaos. None of this has been remotely visible at Celtic for a while.

highlights.title: Resident Evil and Silent Hill Are Just as Cozy as Animal Crossing, According to Science
highlights.summary: You can feel it in the air, can’t you? We’re in the last couple weeks of summer, and spooky season is just around the corner. Zach Cregger’s new Resident Evil movie is getting rave reviews — including from us! So long swimming pools and barbecues, the people demand thrills and chills.
body: To learn more about the appeal of cozy horror, I spoke with affective neuroscientist Dr. Eric Leonardis, who’s an expert in how our brains process emotions through play and entertainment. (He previously weighed in on one of our most-anticipated fall games, Virtue and a Sledgehammer.) In the eyes of the good doctor, it’s all about taking back control.

“It's what they call dark play in the [neuroscientific] literature, this idea that if you have these explorations of negative themes, sometimes doing so will actually make you feel like you have more control over what might happen in the future,” Leonardis explained. “Because we've simulated it, we've thought it through, right? The classic example is like when Michael Myers comes up the stairs, and you're like, don't go into the basement, go out the front door. Get out of there. You know what I mean? This is what I would do in this situation, right? And that can be comforting.”
He adds that horror can feel cozy because we know we are safe in the heat of the moment, even if our character is getting their neck ripped open by a vicious zombie.

It was Kardashian’s first time visiting the London store, following its soft opening in July. Naturally, she dressed for the occasion. She wore Ludovic de Saint Sernin’s Mermaid Bi Dress in flesh-toned leather, which closely contoured her curves with a grommet-studded bodice and lace-up slit revealing a sheer underlay beneath. The choice was particularly apt: Kardashian’s forthcoming collaboration with the designer is set to launch October 1, marrying Skims’s shapewear foundations with Saint Sernin’s unapologetically sexy, party-ready signatures. Later, she shimmied into a sculpted chocolate brown corset with belted and tie-up detailing and a hip-skimming maxi skirt.

videos.title: CFB Week 3 REACTION! Ole Miss KNOCKS OFF LSU, Kentucky SHOCKS Texas A&M, Vanderbilt MADNESS | SVPod
videos.summary: Scott Van Pelt and Stanford Steve give their LSU-Ole Miss reaction, Alabama-Florida State reaction, Kentucky-Texas A&M reaction, Mississippi State-South Carolina reaction, Louisville-SMU reaction and more.
body: Also, discussion on Virginia Tech-Maryland, Miami-Wake Forest, Texas Tech-Houston, Georgia-Arkansas, Florida-Auburn, Michigan-UTEP, Oregon-Portland State, USC-Rutgers, Oklahoma-New Mexico, Texas-UTSA, West Virginia-Virginia and plenty more from Week 3, including Steve’s first-hand experience doing College GameDay with Morgan Freeman and seeing Oxford in the days leading up to the game.
points: Scott Van Pelt and Stanford Steve give their LSU-Ole Miss reaction, Alabama-Florida State reaction, Kentucky-Texas A&M reaction, Mississippi State-South Carolina reaction, Louisville-SMU reaction and…
Plus, the guys discuss one of the worst bad beats of all time between Vanderbilt and NC State in Nashville.
Also, discussion on Virginia Tech-Maryland, Miami-Wake Forest, Texas Tech-Houston, Georgia-Arkansas, Florida-Auburn, Michigan-UTEP, Oregon-Portland State, USC-Rutgers, Oklahoma-New Mexico…
